Qxd8 is not legal? That's strange. Let me think about why. The queen is on e4, the rook is on d8. The queen should be able to move diagonally or horizontally from e4 to d8... wait, d8 is not reachable from e4 by a queen's move!

A queen can move horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. From e4:
- Horizontal (4th rank): a4, b4, c4, d4, f4, g4, h4
- Vertical (e-file): e1, e2, e3, e5, e6, e7, e8
- Diagonal: d3, c2, b1 (southwest), f3, g2, h1 (southeast), d5, c6, b7, a8 (northwest), f5, g6, h7 (northeast)

So from e4, the queen cannot reach d8. d8 is not on any of these lines. So Qxd8 is indeed not legal.

OK so after Rd8 Rxd8 (e8-rook takes), White cannot play Qxd8. White would have to play something else like Qxb7 or other moves.

This suggests that Rd8 directly (without Qxe8+ first) is not the best move because after Rxd8, White doesn't have a good follow-up.

But Qxe8+ FIRST removes the e8-rook from defending. So after Qxe8+ Rxe8, the f8-rook is now on e8. Then Rd8 attacks the f8-rook (now on e8) and threatens Rxe8#.

After Qxe8+ Rxe8 Rd8, White threatens Rxe8+. Black must either play Rxd8 (sacrificing the rook) or lose the rook to Rxe8.

So Qxe8+ is the key first move because it forces the f8-rook to e8, and then Rd8 creates the threat.
